chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about jewelry (gold ornaments), whether there is zakat in it? He said: 'No, except what is removed from the zakat (i.e., what is exempted or taken out as the zakat portion).'

key_terms.الْحُلِيِّ: Jewelry (specifically gold ornaments worn by women)
key_terms.زَكَاةٌ: Alms-tax (obligatory payment of a specific portion of wealth)
key_terms.فُرَّ بِهِ: What is removed/exempted (referring to the zakat portion taken out)

ai.seo_question: Is there zakat on gold jewelry in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific ruling on gold jewelry (*al-huliy*), distinguishing between the ornament itself and the wealth component. The phrase 'except what is removed from the zakat' indicates that the jewelry is exempt from zakat unless it constitutes a distinct store of wealth (savings) that meets the *nisab* and *hawl* conditions, rather than being worn for adornment. This highlights the Shia juristic principle of differentiating between consumable/ornamental use and capital accumulation in zakat calculations.
